one_line_contribution: A controlled measurement of whether reader-side read-time reconstruction of retrieved experience buys anything over token-matched verbatim injection, as a function of who wrote the experience — with writer policy distance (scaffold, temperature) and writer capability (thinking mode) manipulated separately inside one backbone, plus a cross-backbone reversal.
closest_prior_work: Two verified threats. (1) arXiv:2605.30723, 'Skill is Not One-Size-Fits-All: Model-Aware Skill Alignment for LLM Agents' (2026-05-29; verified via the s2cli literature command, hf channel, returned by my query 1). It already establishes the proposal's premise as a result, not an assumption: skill/experience utility is backbone-dependent, and a model-conditioned rewriter that adapts the item to the target backbone recovers the loss. That is 'rewriting foreign experience for the reader is what makes it pay'. It does not threaten the proposal fatally because its rewriter is trained, the writer is not manipulated as a factor, there is no self-pool-at-matched-cost control, no token-matched verbatim comparator, and no proximity-vs-capability decomposition — but it is the nearest published method and, damningly, the proposal's Related Work and Preprint Collision Check never mention it even though the brief names it as a candidate reimplementation. A reviewer who knows this paper will read the proposal as measuring the boundary condition of an already-published effect. (2) arXiv:2607.28272 MemHarness (2026-07-30; verified with `s2cli.py paper`), whose thesis is exactly 'memory is reconstructed, not replayed' and which reports reconstruction preventing negative transfer; the proposal correctly notes its retrieval is self-written and its policy GRPO-trained, and reimplements it training-free as C_r3. Also relevant and not cited: arXiv:2602.11220, 'Patch the Distribution Mismatch: RL Rewriting Agent for Stable Off-Policy SFT' (verified with `s2cli.py paper`), which is the training-time analogue of the same mechanism — rewriting off-policy data into the consumer model's own distribution, with the gain governed by distributional mismatch. In the home literature the mechanism is older still: arXiv:2211.06839 (Out-of-Dynamics Imitation Learning: demonstrations from different demonstrators must be screened for transferability) and arXiv:2210.08073 (Eliciting Compatible Demonstrations: demonstrator-learner compatibility, not demonstrator skill, governs demonstration value) already say 'the value of a demonstration depends on the demonstrator's distance from the learner'. So the mechanism is not new; what is new is measuring the adaptation increment as a function of a manipulated writer at matched consumer tokens.
strongest_objection: The design is pre-registered to be underpowered for its own headline. Every prediction P1-P4 and P7-P8 is a difference of two paired differences of reconstruction increments, required to exceed M = max(G0/3, h_DiD) ≈ 6.5 WITH a CI excluding 0 — i.e. the point estimate must land near 12 net success points. A reconstruction increment over an already-strong k=7 verbatim arm is a second-order effect; nothing in the measured record on this node (k7 - k3 = +2.3) or in MemHarness-scale reported gains suggests that D itself will be more than a few points, let alone that two D's will differ by 12. Worse, the power arithmetic that makes the margin look attainable is wrong in kind: the ±8 noise floor at 274 games x 2 seeds is a game-clustered bootstrap half-width, whose dominant term is between-game variance, and the readers run at T=0. Adding seeds shrinks only the within-game sampling component, which for a deterministic reader on a fixed game set is small; the assumed 1/sqrt(seeds) scaling from ±8 to ±4 (and ±5.7 for a DiD) is therefore optimistic, quite possibly by a lot. The proposal's own floor M >= h_DiD makes this self-defeating rather than self-correcting: if h_DiD stays near 8, M rises to 8 and the required point estimate rises to ~16 net, so the harder the noise, the more unpassable the prediction. The overwhelmingly likely outcome of ~58k episodes is a page of intervals that straddle the margin, at which point the pre-registered fallback ('report the absolute per-cell increments, P5') reduces the paper to a training-free MemHarness replication in two cells — with the writer manipulation, the entire contribution, unreportable. Two secondary flaws compound it: P3, the arm that carries the 'not writer capability' half of the title, is pre-confessed as likely confounded (thinking mode changes phrasing and trace length as well as capability, and the design's own escape is 'report as confounded' if W_cap's JS divergence exceeds W_scaf's); and P8, the arm that separates translation from compression, degenerates when Gate 0 falls back to W_far = W_exp, because the expert bank is already inside the 2x-median cap, so P8 then differs from P1 only in the self cell.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Fix the power argument before the margins: decompose the existing Measurement C 2-seed data into between-game and within-game (seed) variance components and report what an 8-seed cluster-bootstrap half-width actually is, instead of assuming 1/sqrt(seeds); if the game term dominates (it will, at T=0), buy precision by adding evaluation games from the 3,553 train pool held out of every bank, not by adding seeds. 2) Re-anchor the margin to a plausible increment (a DiD of 4-6 net, powered) rather than to one third of the verbatim gain, which is a margin for a first-order effect being applied to a second-order one. 3) Remove the ceiling asymmetry: D(W_far) and D(W_self) are increments measured at very different C_v7 baselines (0.81/0.87 on the expert bank), so analyze on the per-game subset where C_v7 fails, or on a logit/odds scale, and report the matched-difficulty contrast as the headline. 4) Build W_cap with action-template divergence matched to W_scaf by construction — force thinking-mode traces through the standard action template so only capability moves — instead of gating on an ordering that the design admits may not hold. 5) Build a capped foreign bank distinct from W_exp so P8 is non-degenerate under the Gate-0 fallback, and state P8 as its own DiD with its own margin so it survives an indeterminate P1. 6) Score C_pl_mis against the matched-type C_r3 cell rather than against static3, so the second clause of P6 can actually come out against the hypothesis. 7) Add the omitted baselines below.
missing_baseline: An offline, write-time rewrite of the foreign bank into the reader's action grammar — each item translated once at bank-construction time, then retrieved verbatim at k=3/k=7 — plus a mechanical action-template remap (string-level translation of verb/argument patterns into the reader's grammar, no LLM planning). The plan contrasts only per-episode read-time reconstruction against verbatim injection, so a positive D establishes at most that translation somewhere in the pipeline pays; it cannot support the paper's practical recommendation, because the amortized offline arm costs one rewrite per item instead of one rewrite per episode and is the arm any practitioner would run first. If the offline rewrite captures the increment, the 'read-time, first-observation-conditioned' framing is dead and only the reconstruct-every-5-steps ablation remains interesting. The mechanical remap is equally load-bearing: C_pl_static (rewriting fixed correct exemplars) controls for 'planning helps', but nothing in the plan separates 'the foreign item was translated into my grammar' from 'an LLM synthesized a fresh plan from foreign content'. Secondary omission: the brief names the model-conditioned skill rewriter (2605.30723) as a reimplementable transfer method and it is the closest published competitor; only MemHarness-without-RL is reimplemented.

I did not verify 2608.07169, 2604.14004, 2604.07487 or 2609.01437, which the proposal leans on only lightly. Judgment of the proposal's own check: it is above average for this round — four classed queries, IDs given for every hit, one ID verified with the `paper` subcommand, and an explicit statement of what the nearest pre-emption (AdaCoM) does not do. Its defect is a specific one, not vagueness: it omits 2605.30723, the model-conditioned skill rewriter that the brief itself lists as the closest reimplementable method and that already reports the model-dependence of skill utility and a rewriter that fixes it, and it omits the off-policy-rewriting literature (2602.11220) that is the training-time twin of its mechanism. An author who searched the mechanism's home vocabulary as instructed should have surfaced the demonstrator-compatibility results (2211.06839, 2210.08073), which show the conceptual claim is not new outside text agents; the novelty that remains is measurement, not mechanism.
